cues: The other half of question four: a story from outline notes.
Read every note first; you cannot choose an opening until you know the ending.
Fill in what the notes leave out, a name, a place, a season, without contradicting any note.
Choose past tense and third person, and hold them.
Weight the notes unequally: the turning point gets four or five sentences, the setting two.
Show rather than tell: not he was frightened, but he put the bag down twice before he could untie it.
Add a line or two of direct speech.
And a short title that does not give away the ending.
